newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended lower across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Thursday.
The news of the death of the China's Deng Xiaoping had little impact on the market.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly today after a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-3/4 3-5/8 percent versus Wednesday's 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent.

Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.63/98.68 compared with Wednesday's close of S$98.70/98.75, September 2001 at S$97.30/97.35 against S$97.42/97.47 and June 2003 at S$95.28/95.33 from S$95.40/95.45.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.40/1.35 percent against Wednesday's yield of 1.20/1.15 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.85/1.80 percent from 1.75/1.70 percent.
